No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I estimated the largest off-resonant SHG coefficient from:

- whether the atomic arrangement appears centrosymmetric, in which case electric-dipole SHG is zero;
- anion polarizability, approximately Te > Se > S > halides;
- polar alignment of tetrahedral or pyramidal units;
- electronically active Cu, Ag, Tl, Hg, Sb, and lone-pair cations;
- cancellation caused by antiparallel or highly symmetric substructures.

The resulting point estimates are approximate—often uncertain by at least a factor of two without electronic-structure calculations.
